title: GS21 exposure U-SHAPED IN LEVERAGE with a continuous firm-level debt capacity: coupon drawn at birth from [0.1, 0.9] (gs_fixcs 2), exposure 0.1 (b~^2 - 1), one type, price 2.5
question: Does the distress-and-rationing story (cash-flow exposure U-shaped in leverage) give GS21 room and a fair gap at the bar when leverage is a continuous, exogenous firm attribute rather than a few observed groups?
notes:
WHY (2026-11-02). The leverage U with a firm-level, continuously drawn debt capacity. The fixed-coupon TYPES (gvylu30/30c) had no room because three perfectly observed groups with very different equity values are priced linearly through leverage and book-to-market; endogenous leverage (gvyql) spans 0.002-0.006 across quintiles. Here every firm draws its coupon per unit capital at birth uniformly from the 16 grid nodes in [0.1, 0.9] and keeps it (gs_fixcs 2), so leverage varies continuously across firms, independently of productivity, as productivity itself does. The exposure to y is gs_bv (b~^2 - 1), b~ = (b - 0.5)/0.29 the standardized coupon: mean about zero across firms, U-shaped in leverage, the story being that highly levered firms are in distress and lowly levered firms are credit-rationed, both more exposed to the aggregate cash-flow shock than the middle. gs_bv 0.1.

PRECOMMITMENT STATUS: precommitted=false; ids filled from the Quest build log by the solve script before any seed runs.

PREDICTION (2026-11-02): the premium across leverage quintiles is U-shaped; room 30% or more and a fair gap at or above +0.029 (gvyzzh10's productivity quadratic: 70%, +0.080). FALSIFIED if room is at or below 10% on three seeds.
